transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I'm really only sitting here because my family and my friends wouldn't leave me alone about it. They keep shoving these... these bank papers in my face. They printed out all these statements, like a whole thick stack of them, and they keep pointing at the lines and the numbers and saying it proves nothing was taken. But I know what I know. I'm not blind, and I'm not stupid. 

For over a year now—a whole year, day in and day out—I've known for an absolute fact that they are hiding my money. And they think they're being so smart about it, too, like I can't see what's happening right in front of me. They use all these little tricks and excuses to cover it up. Like, suddenly my cousin is doing this big "fundraiser" online and needs everyone to donate, or my friend is making all these fancy trip plans to go out of state and talking about booking hotels, or they talk about all these random "bills" that just magically had to be paid. It's all a front! They just shuffle my money around and put it into the fundraiser, or the vacation fund, or these fake bills so I can't track where it went. 

So they wanted me to come talk to you because they want me to just drop it. But I'm not going to drop it. I have to keep confronting them. I call them, I show up at their houses, I bring it up every single time I see them, and I'm going to keep getting in their faces about it until they finally break down and tell me the truth about what they did.
Have you ever seen, heard, or sensed things that others don't seem to notice, like voices or presences, that made you feel like your money was being taken?

Voices? No. No, I don't... I don't know why you'd even ask me about ghosts or whispers or whatever. I don't hear anything like that. I don't need some voice in my head to tell me what my own two eyes can see perfectly fine, you know? 

I mean, think about it. If I was hearing things, they'd probably just use that against me too, right? They'd say, oh, she's hearing voices, don't listen to her, she doesn't know what she's talking about. But I don't. I don't see shadows or, or presences sneaking into my room at night to steal my wallet. It's not some invisible spirit taking my cash, it's my own cousin! It's my friends! I don't need a magical voice to tell me that my cousin suddenly has five hundred dollars for a charity walk when she hasn't even had a job since last November. You see what I mean? 

I don't hear voices because I don't need to hear them. The proof is right there on their internet pages, in the way they look at each other when I walk into the room, in the way they get all quiet when I ask them about the hotel prices. It's real life, not some made-up spooky story from a movie. So no, no voices, no presences, nothing like that at all. Just real people doing real sneaky things right behind my back, and I don't need anyone whispering in my ear to figure that out.
Have you ever had a belief that something physically impossible was happening, like money being stolen through supernatural or unreal means?

Supernatural? Unreal means? No, no, no, I just told you, it's not ghosts or magic or aliens beaming my money up to a spaceship! I don't know why you keep trying to make it sound like I'm crazy or like I think I'm living in some kind of sci-fi movie. I'm talking about regular, everyday bank transfers, cash apps, maybe they got my routing number—I mean, I left my purse on the kitchen counter at my sister's house on Thanksgiving, and my cousin was right there in the living room, and she had her phone out. She could have easily just snapped a picture of my debit card or written down the numbers on a napkin or something. That's not supernatural, that's just basic theft! 

I don't think they're using witchcraft to make my money disappear into thin air. I think they're logging into their little apps and hitting "transfer" or going to the ATM when I'm not looking. It's so frustrating because every time I try to explain this, people act like I'm saying they're using mind control. I'm not! I'm saying they are sneaky, manipulative liars who know exactly how to work the system. Like, remember when I said my friend was planning that trip? She was talking about booking a flight to Florida, and I know for a fact flights to Florida are at least three hundred dollars, and she works part-time at a coffee shop! Where is she getting three hundred dollars? Not from a magic spell, I can tell you that. She's getting it from me. 

So no, I don't believe in anything physically impossible. I believe in math. I believe that if I had money in my account, and now I don't, and suddenly they have extra money for charities and vacations, the math adds up. It's just moving from point A to point B. There's no supernatural anything happening here, just plain old stealing, and I just need someone to actually look at the facts instead of asking me if I believe in magic tricks.
Do you ever feel like your belief about your money being taken is something you just know deep down, even if others say there’s no proof or evidence to support it?

Deep down? No, it's not... I don't know why you're calling it a belief, or saying there's no proof. I just spent this whole time telling you about the proof! It's not some gut feeling I have, like, oh, my stomach hurts so I must be getting robbed. No! It's right there in front of my face. 

They are the ones saying there's no proof. My mom, my sister, they all sit there at the kitchen table—this was just last Tuesday, actually, they had me over for dinner, they made meatloaf, and then they just ambushed me with it again. They slapped these bank statements down right next to my plate and said, "Look, look, the numbers match, there's no evidence anything is missing." But I didn't even finish junior high and I can tell you the numbers don't add up the way they say they do! They think just because I dropped out in the eighth grade that I can't do basic addition, or that I can't read between the lines, but I'm not stupid. I know how to count. 

I don't just "know it deep down." I know it because I see it happening in the real world. I see my cousin buying things. I see the fundraiser pages. If it was just a feeling, I wouldn't be driving over to their houses, knocking on their doors, demanding my cash back. You don't do all that over a feeling. You do that when you have facts. And they can say "there's no evidence" all they want, they can say it until they are completely blue in the face, but that's just what guilty people say, isn't it? 

Think about it, when somebody gets caught doing something wrong, what's the very first thing they say? "You can't prove it." "Where's your proof." That is exactly what my friend said when I called her out about the Florida trip on the phone. She got all defensive, her voice got real high-pitched, and she was like, "You have no proof I took your money!" Well, if you didn't take it, why are you talking about proof? Why not just say you didn't do it? See? It's not a belief. It's a fact. I don't need some "deep down" feeling in my heart when I have my eyes wide open and I can see exactly what they're doing with my own money.
Even though your family and friends have shown you bank statements that they say prove nothing was taken, do you still believe, without any doubt, that your money has been stolen by them?

Without a doubt? Yes! Absolutely without a single doubt in my mind. I mean, that is exactly why I came in here, because my family and my friends, they just keep ganging up on me and saying that these bank papers prove nothing was taken. They just print out these little sheets of paper and point at the black and white lines and say, "See? It's all accounted for, you're making a big deal out of nothing." But I know what's really going on. 

I've known for over a year now. A whole year, actually over a year, of them sneaking around behind my back, and they think they're so smart. They think I don't realize that they're just hiding my money and using all these everyday things to cover it up. Like, they'll say they have a sudden, massive electric bill they had to pay, or they'll set up one of those online fundraisers for a charity walk, or they'll start planning a big trip to Florida, just like I was telling you about with my friend. It's all a smokescreen! They take my cash, they funnel it into these... these trip plans and fake bills, and then they point at the bank statement like that makes it okay. They think because they washed it through a charity page that I won't recognize it's my own money paying for their vacations!

So no, I don't have any doubts. None at all. And I'm not just gonna let it go, either. I can't. I have to keep confronting them. I'm going to keep showing up at their houses, I'm going to keep calling them out on the phone, asking the hard questions, pushing them on it until they finally break down and tell the truth. I don't care how many times they wave a bank statement in my face. They know exactly what they did, and I know what they did, and I'm not going to stop being in their faces about it until they admit it and give me every single dime back.
